## Natural history notes

A medium-sized tachinid fly characterized by a dark body, orange to reddish abdomen, smoky wings, and distinctive feather-like fringes on the hind legs. In Florida, the Swift Feather-legged Fly is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, farms, roadsides, and other open or semi-open habitats where flowers and true bug hosts are common. Adults visit flowers for nectar, while females lay eggs on stink bugs, leaf-footed bugs, and squash bugs; the fly larva develops inside the host, making this species an important natural enemy of several plant-feeding bugs.
